title: Legislating Need for Motorists to Report Traffic Accidents to Their Insurers
what_it_is: Legislating Need for Motorists to Report Traffic Accidents to Their Insurers

sections.label: Motor Claims Framework reporting rules
sections.summary: The GIA Motor Claims Framework requires accidents to be reported to insurers within 24 hours or the next working day, but insurers cannot refuse liability for non-reporting under the Motor Vehicle (Third Party Risks and Compensation) Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The General Insurance Association of Singapore (GIA)'s Motor Claims Framework (MCF) sets out the procedures for all accidents to be reported to the insurer within 24 hours or by the next working day, which is incorporated as a condition of all motor insurance policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the above, under the Motor Vehicle (Third Party Risks and Compensation) Act, an insurer cannot refuse liability on the ground that the policyholder has not reported the accident.

sections.label: Review of accident reporting requirements
sections.summary: MOT, LTA and MAS will work with other Government agencies and GIA to review and, if necessary, strengthen requirements for reporting road traffic accidents to insurers.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The Ministry of Transport (MOT), LTA and MAS will work with other relevant Government agencies and GIA to review and, if necessary, strengthen the requirements for reporting road traffic accidents to insurers.

sections.label: GIA referral facility
sections.summary: Amongst the GIA, there is a facility where such cases are referred to.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Amongst the GIA, there is a facility where such cases are referred to.

sections.label: Reporting incentives and undisputed matters
sections.summary: These matters are never undisputed, so Government action must be based on disclosed facts, and motorists have incentives to report because failing to do so risks losing insurance cover, without which driving is unlawful.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The first is that these matters are never undisputed.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, ex ante, there is no case that just because one party has the details of the other party, it means the other party is the offender or the "culprit" – in the words of Member.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, any action taken by any Government organisation in terms of investigation or follow-up has to be meritorious, has to be on the basis that there are facts disclosed that point to that.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Having said that, the key point here is, first, the incentives are actually there, by and large, for motorists to make such reports in compliance with their contract; because if the insurers were to find that they did not make such a report and subsequently, there are claims made and there is a set of issues, then for the party concerned, the risk is that they stand to lose their insurance cover and, without insurance cover, you cannot drive a vehicle on the roads according to our laws.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But again, ultimately, no matter what the mandatory requirements are, the system functions best when all parties concerned are aware of their obligations under the law and fulfil those obligations.
